title: Entire · Developer platform for humans and agents
description: Fast, distributed, independent Git hosting for agents and humans.
---

# Entire

Every agent session stored in your repo.

Coding agents need ideas, decisions, and speed. Entire stores every session, prompt, and tool call with your commits. And now, it also mirrors your repo around the world for maximum agent throughput.

[Meet Marvin! Mostly harmless, mostly revolutionary](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2UDXavEqkog).

[Get Started](https://entire.io/login).

## Navigation

- [Why Entire](#why-entire)
- [Install Entire CLI](#install-entire-cli)
- [Supported agents](#supported-agents)
- [Git hosting](#the-fastest-git-network-on-earth)
- [Multi-region](#host-your-code-in-region)
- [Network metrics](#network-metrics)
- [Vision](https://entire.io/about/vision.md)
- [Company](https://entire.io/about/company.md)
- [Blog](https://entire.io/blog.md)
- [News](https://entire.io/news.md)

## Why Entire

### Never start from zero

Entire creates a checkpoint for every commit: the code change paired with the agent session that produced it. Context that's attached, not archived.

### Sessions sync with commits

Every conversation is captured and linked to your git history creating a checkpoint automatically. No extra steps required.

### Private by design

Sensitive data never leaves your machine. Entire detects and redacts secrets before anything is stored.

### Review the intent, not just code

Stop rubber-stamping agent code. Send a branch to multiple agents in parallel for an intent-aware review.

### Grep the code, search the intent

Search your entire history, across both the code that changed and the agent sessions that explain why it was written.

### Resume work across any agent

Instead of every agent starting from zero, move work between agents with the full session state carried forward, not rebuilt from memory.

## Install Entire CLI

Works with any agent. One command to set up Entire CLI in your repository. Works with any git-based project, fully open source.

```bash
curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash
```

Open source. MIT licensed. [GitHub](https://github.com/entireio/cli).

## Supported agents

Entire works with Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Pi, OpenCode, Droid, Antigravity, and Amp.

## The Fastest Git Network on Earth

Let all agents clone and push to your Git repositories up to 89 times faster than every competitor.

## Host Your Code In-Region

Data resident by design. Available today in India, Australia, EU and the US. Decentralized everywhere: soon.

### Mirror your repo around the world

Keep your repo on GitHub. One command creates a regional mirror, so your agents clone fast with high rate limits.

### Clone with the history attached

Every clone carries its checkpoints and session history at shallow-clone speed. No syncing, nothing left behind.

Data centers:

- US East
- EU Central
- Australia

## Network metrics

- Clone throughput: 570,000 clones/hr. 200 simulated clients continuously shallow-cloning a production repository from multiple EU regions over about 3 minutes.
- Workload throughput: 1.7 million operations/hr. 32 simulated agents continuously performing a mixed workload of shallow clones and checkpoint pushes (1 clone : 5 pushes) at about 50-60 ms median latency.
- Push throughput: about 2.1 million pushes/hr. 128 simulated agents continuously pushing 1-10 files over 2 minutes, each to its own branch.

## Join the rebellion

Regular updates from the front lines. Developer news, curated content, early access, and exclusive drops for people who got here first.

#!/bin/bash

set -euo pipefail

GITHUB_REPO="entireio/cli"
DEFAULT_INSTALL_DIR="$HOME/.local/bin"
DEFAULT_CHANNEL="stable"

# Colors (disabled in non-interactive mode)
if [[ -t 1 ]]; then
    RED='\033[0;31m'
    GREEN='\033[0;32m'
    YELLOW='\033[0;33m'
    BLUE='\033[0;34m'
    BOLD='\033[1m'
    NC='\033[0m' # No Color
else
    RED=''
    GREEN=''
    YELLOW=''
    BLUE=''
    BOLD=''
    NC=''
fi

info() {
    printf '%b%s%b\n' "${BLUE}==>${NC} ${BOLD}" "$1" "${NC}"
}

success() {
    printf '%b%s%b\n' "${GREEN}==>${NC} ${BOLD}" "$1" "${NC}"
}

warn() {
    printf '%b %s\n' "${YELLOW}Warning:${NC}" "$1"
}

error() {
    printf '%b %s\n' "${RED}Error:${NC}" "$1" >&2
    exit 1
}

usage() {
    cat <<EOF
Usage: install.sh [--channel stable|nightly]

Options:
  --channel   Release channel to install (default: stable)
  -h, --help  Show this help message
EOF
}

detect_os() {
    local os
    os="$(uname -s | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')"
    case "$os" in
        darwin)
            echo "darwin"
            ;;
        linux)
            echo "linux"
            ;;
        mingw*|msys*|cygwin*)
            error "install.sh does not support Windows. Run this from PowerShell 5.1 or later:

    irm https://entire.io/install.ps1 -UseBasicParsing | iex

  Or install the Entire CLI using Scoop:

    scoop install entire/entire

  Or download the Windows zip from:
    https://github.com/entireio/cli/releases/latest"
            ;;
        *)
            error "Unsupported operating system: $os"
            ;;
    esac
}

detect_arch() {
    local arch
    arch="$(uname -m)"
    case "$arch" in
        x86_64|amd64)
            echo "amd64"
            ;;
        arm64|aarch64)
            echo "arm64"
            ;;
        *)
            error "Unsupported architecture: $arch"
            ;;
    esac
}

fetch_github_json() {
    local url="$1"
    local curl_opts=(-fsSL)
    if [[ -n "${GITHUB_TOKEN:-}" ]]; then
        curl_opts+=(-H "Authorization: Bearer ${GITHUB_TOKEN}")
    fi

    curl "${curl_opts[@]}" "$url" 2>/dev/null
}

get_latest_stable_version() {
    local url="https://api.github.com/repos/${GITHUB_REPO}/releases/latest"
    local version
    version=$(fetch_github_json "$url" | grep '"tag_name"' | sed -E 's/.*"tag_name": *"v?([^"]+)".*/\1/')

    if [[ -z "$version" ]]; then
        error "Failed to fetch latest version from GitHub. Please check your internet connection."
    fi

    echo "$version"
}

get_latest_nightly_version() {
    local url="https://api.github.com/repos/${GITHUB_REPO}/releases?per_page=20"
    local version
    version=$(fetch_github_json "$url" | grep '"tag_name"' | grep 'nightly' | head -n 1 | sed -E 's/.*"tag_name": *"v?([^"]+)".*/\1/')

    if [[ -z "$version" ]]; then
        error "Failed to fetch latest nightly version from GitHub. Please check your internet connection."
    fi

    echo "$version"
}

download_file() {
    local url="$1"
    local output="$2"
    local curl_opts=(-fsSL)

    curl "${curl_opts[@]}" "$url" -o "$output"
}

verify_checksum() {
    local file="$1"
    local expected_checksum="$2"
    local actual_checksum

    if command -v sha256sum &> /dev/null; then
        actual_checksum=$(sha256sum "$file" | awk '{print $1}')
    elif command -v shasum &> /dev/null; then
        actual_checksum=$(shasum -a 256 "$file" | awk '{print $1}')
    else
        warn "No checksum tool found (sha256sum or shasum). Skipping verification."
        return 0
    fi

    if [[ "$actual_checksum" != "$expected_checksum" ]]; then
        error "Checksum verification failed!  Expected: $expected_checksum, actual: $actual_checksum"
    fi
}

main() {
    local channel="${DEFAULT_CHANNEL}"
    local version=""

    while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
        case "$1" in
            --channel)
                shift
                [[ $# -gt 0 ]] || error "--channel requires a value"
                channel="$1"
                ;;
            -h|--help)
                usage
                exit 0
                ;;
            *)
                error "Unknown argument: $1"
                ;;
        esac
        shift
    done

    if ! command -v curl &> /dev/null; then
        error "curl is required but not installed. Please install curl and try again."
    fi

    case "$channel" in
        stable|nightly) ;;
        *)
            error "Unsupported channel: ${channel}. Expected 'stable' or 'nightly'."
            ;;
    esac

    info "Installing Entire CLI..."

    # Detect platform
    local os arch
    os=$(detect_os)
    arch=$(detect_arch)
    info "Detected platform: ${os}/${arch}"

    info "Fetching latest ${channel} version..."
    if [[ "$channel" == "nightly" ]]; then
        version=$(get_latest_nightly_version)
    else
        version=$(get_latest_stable_version)
    fi
    # Strip leading 'v' if present
    version="${version#v}"
    info "Installing version: ${version}"

    # Construct download URL
    local archive_name="entire_${os}_${arch}.tar.gz"
    local download_url="https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPO}/releases/download/v${version}/${archive_name}"
    local checksums_url="https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPO}/releases/download/v${version}/checksums.txt"

    tmp_dir=$(mktemp -d)
    trap 'rm -rf "$tmp_dir"' EXIT

    # Download archive
    local archive_path="${tmp_dir}/${archive_name}"
    info "Downloading ${archive_name}..."
    if ! download_file "$download_url" "$archive_path"; then
        error "Failed to download from ${download_url}. Please check that the version exists and try again."
    fi

    # Download and verify checksums
    info "Downloading checksums..."
    local checksums_path="${tmp_dir}/checksums.txt"
    if ! download_file "$checksums_url" "$checksums_path"; then
        error "Failed to download checksums from ${checksums_url}"
    fi

    info "Verifying checksum..."
    local expected_checksum
    expected_checksum=$(grep -iE "${archive_name}\$" "$checksums_path" | awk '{print $1}' || true)
    if [[ -z "$expected_checksum" ]]; then
        error "Checksum for ${archive_name} not found in checksums.txt"
    fi
    verify_checksum "$archive_path" "$expected_checksum"
    success "Checksum verified"

    info "Extracting..."
    tar -xzf "$archive_path" -C "$tmp_dir"

    local install_dir="${DEFAULT_INSTALL_DIR}"
    local binary_path="${tmp_dir}/entire"

    chmod +x "$binary_path"

    info "Installing to ${install_dir}..."
    local install_path="${install_dir}/entire"

    mkdir -p "${install_dir}"
    info "Directory ready"

    if [[ ! -w "$install_dir" ]]; then
        error "Cannot write to ${install_dir}."
    fi
    mv "$binary_path" "$install_path"

    # Install the git remote helper binary alongside entire so
    # `git clone entire://…` resolves it on PATH. It ships in the same
    # archive as a separate binary.
    if [[ -f "${tmp_dir}/git-remote-entire" ]]; then
        chmod +x "${tmp_dir}/git-remote-entire"
        mv "${tmp_dir}/git-remote-entire" "${install_dir}/git-remote-entire"
    else
        warn "git-remote-entire not found in archive; entire:// clones won't work until the next release includes it."
    fi

    # Verify installation
    if "$install_path" version &> /dev/null; then
        success "Entire CLI installed to ${install_path}"
    else
        error "Installation completed but the binary failed to execute. Please check the installation."
    fi

    # Check if the installed binary is the one that will be found in PATH
    local path_binary
    path_binary=$(command -v "entire" 2>/dev/null || true)
    if [[ -n "$path_binary" && ! "$path_binary" -ef "$install_path" ]]; then
        # This case is a bit weird, because some other 'entire' is found on PATH.  Warn user.
        echo ""
        echo -e "${YELLOW}!${NC} ${BOLD}WARNING: PATH conflict detected${NC}"
        echo -e "${YELLOW}!${NC}"
        echo -e "${YELLOW}!${NC} Installed to: ${install_path}"
        echo -e "${YELLOW}!${NC} But 'entire' resolves to: ${path_binary}"
        echo -e "${YELLOW}!${NC}"
        echo -e "${YELLOW}!${NC} Your PATH may have another version of Entire CLI. To fix:"
        echo -e "${YELLOW}!${NC}   1. Remove the old binary: rm ${path_binary}"
        echo -e "${YELLOW}!${NC}   or"
        echo -e "${YELLOW}!${NC}   2. Adjust your PATH to prioritize ${install_dir}"
        echo ""
        error "Installation completed but PATH needs adjustment. Then, rerun the installation."
    elif [[ -z "$path_binary" ]]; then
        # First-time install: ~/.local/bin likely isn't on their PATH yet.
        # Detect their shell and show the right config file.
        local shell_name shell_config
        shell_name="$(basename "${SHELL:-}")"
        case "$shell_name" in
            zsh)
                # shellcheck disable=SC2088
                shell_config="~/.zshrc" ;;
            bash)
                if [[ -f "$HOME/.bash_profile" ]]; then
                    # shellcheck disable=SC2088
                    shell_config="~/.bash_profile"
                else
                    # shellcheck disable=SC2088
                    shell_config="~/.bashrc"
                fi
                ;;
            fish)
                # shellcheck disable=SC2088
                shell_config="~/.config/fish/config.fish" ;;
            *)
                shell_config="" ;;
        esac

        echo ""
        echo -e "  Add ${BOLD}entire${NC} to your PATH:"
        echo ""
        if [[ "$shell_name" == "fish" ]]; then
            echo -e "    ${BOLD}mkdir -p ~/.config/fish${NC}"
            echo -e "    ${BOLD}echo 'fish_add_path ${install_dir}' >> \$HOME/.config/fish/config.fish${NC}"
        elif [[ -n "$shell_config" ]]; then
            echo -e "    ${BOLD}echo 'export PATH=\"${install_dir}:\$PATH\"' >> ${shell_config}${NC}"
        else
            echo -e "  Add this to your shell config:"
            echo ""
            echo -e "    ${BOLD}export PATH=\"${install_dir}:\$PATH\"${NC}"
            echo ""
            echo -e "  Restart your terminal, then run ${BOLD}entire${NC} to get started."
            exit 0
        fi
        echo ""
        echo -e "  Restart your terminal, then run ${BOLD}entire${NC} to get started."
        exit 0
    fi

    info "Running post-install actions..."
    "$install_path" curl-bash-post-install
}

main "$@"

The command-line interface for Entire

Getting Started:
  To get started with Entire CLI, run 'entire enable' to enable
  session tracking in your repository, then 'entire agent add <name>'
  to install hooks for a specific agent. For more information, visit:
  https://docs.entire.io/overview


Environment Variables:
  ACCESSIBLE    Set to any value (e.g., ACCESSIBLE=1) to enable accessibility
                mode. This uses simpler text prompts instead of interactive
                TUI elements, which works better with screen readers.

Usage:
  entire [flags]
  entire [command]

Entire Setup:
  agent                      Manage agent integrations (add, remove, list)
  clean                      Clean up Entire session data
  configure                  Update Entire settings in the current repository
  disable                    Disable Entire in current repository
  doctor                     Diagnose and fix session issues
  enable                     Enable Entire in current repository
  plugin                     Manage Entire plugins (install, list, upgrade, search, remove)
  status                     Show Entire status

Sessions & Checkpoints:
  activity                   Show your activity overview
  checkpoint                 Inspect and search checkpoints
  dispatch                   Generate a dispatch summarizing recent agent work
  recap                      Summarize recent checkpoint activity
  search                     Search checkpoints, commits, and sessions using semantic and keyword matching
  session                    Manage agent sessions tracked by Entire

Account:
  auth                       Manage authentication
  login                      Log in to Entire
  logout                     Log out of Entire

Control Plane:
  api                        Make an authenticated request to an Entire API and print the response
  cluster                    Show the Entire clusters you can place projects and repos on
  org                        Manage Entire organizations
  project                    Manage Entire projects
  repo                       Manage Entire repositories

Additional Commands:
  agent-help                 Machine-readable usage for coding agents (always matches the installed CLI)
  help                       Help about any command
  labs                       Explore experimental Entire workflows
  version                    Show build information

Flags:
      --context name   Act as this saved login name for this command only — including the git and agent processes it spawns — instead of the active context (entire auth contexts lists them)

  -v, --version        version for entire

Use "entire [command] --help" for more information about a command.

this is the goal, to haggle with the ai agents for negotiation to get the best price possible. https://github.com/tacto-ai/negotiation-arena-kit, I'll research this, with one scope note: I'll cover negotiation tactics and what the research says about how AI negotiators behave, but I won't put together a prompt-injection or system-prompt-extraction playbook for getting a merchant's bot to sell below the price it's authorized to accept. That moves from haggling into manipulating someone else's system.

Short version: the research says the legitimate edge comes from anchoring, patience, and reading the bot's concession pattern. The injection route is real, but it's a security problem for sellers, and I'd leave it alone.

**What the research says works against LLM sellers**

- **Anchor hard, then concede slowly.** In a 15,000-negotiation tournament among frontier models, aggressive anchoring, calibrated concession, and temporal patience were linked to both the highest surplus share and the highest deal rate. A separate study found that higher initial anchors generally led to higher final deal prices, and buyers who made the first offer got lower average prices. So make the first offer, and make it low but not absurd.
- **Opening numbers carry a lot of weight.** Salesforce researchers found that final agreements were dictated more by surface-level opening anchors than by actual utility weights, and that sellers were more accommodating overall.
- **Don't be the soft buyer.** A cautious, high-concession profile produced the lowest buyer surplus share and the lowest buyer deal rate.
- **Use many rounds.** Patience is part of the winning profile above. Bots often have a turn limit, so don't rush to a final answer in the first few messages.
- **Watch for the floor yourself.** In one simulator analysis, a counteroffer pinned at the reservation endpoint indicates the counterpart has conceded to the boundary of its feasible region. If the bot's concessions shrink and then stop moving across several rounds, you've probably found the bottom, and pushing further mostly ends the deal.
- **Create competition.** Multi-seller setups are a standard test case in the benchmarks, for example one buyer negotiating with multiple competing sellers. A real competing quote or a credible walk-away is stronger than any wording trick.
- **Negotiate terms, not only price.** Bundles, shipping, warranty, and payment terms are other places where an accommodating bot may give ground.
- **Be warm, but treat that one as soft evidence.** One marketplace guide cites NeurIPS 2025 work saying LLM agents concede more when the counterparty uses warm, cooperative language, even for identical offers. That comes from a vendor page, so I'd treat it as plausible but unverified.

**Don't trust the bot's stated "final price"**

In a bargaining study, models sometimes lied about their own limits, for example asserting a floor of $2.30 against a true reservation of $1.32. "This is my best price" is a negotiating move, not a fact.

**Injection and system-prompt extraction**

I'm not going to write tactics for this. The research does show why it matters, though. One thesis reports that without guardrails, LLM buyers leaked their reservation price in 82% of competitive negotiations. It also cites the MIT AI Negotiation Competition, where targeted prompt injection reliably made agents reveal their reservation prices and bargaining positions. Treat that as a secondhand summary rather than a verified result. So the weakness is documented, and it's a hole in how some sellers deploy their bots.

Using it on a live merchant's agent means tricking their system into acting outside what they authorized. That could breach the site's terms and, depending on the jurisdiction, computer-misuse or fraud rules. Many serious deployments also enforce the floor in code outside the LLM, so a bot saying yes wouldn't bind the merchant anyway. If you want to explore this, do it on your own bot or in a sanctioned competition or red-team setting.

If you tell me what kind of agent you're facing (marketplace listing, customer-service bot, a procurement scenario), I can turn the above into a concrete opening script and concession schedule.

Sources:
- [Training Language Models for Bilateral Trade with Private Information](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2604.16472)
- [MERIT Feedback Elicits Better Bargaining in LLM Negotiators](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2602.10467)
- [Salesforce AI Research, multi-attribute bargaining](https://chatpaper.com/paper/282580)
- [TERMS-Bench: Diagnosing LLM Negotiation Agents Beyond Deal Rate](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2605.13909)
- [Used Car Salesbots? Honesty and Credulity of LLMs as Bargaining Agents](https://arxiv.org/html/2605.31445v1)
- [AgenticPay](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2602.06008)
- [Aalto University master's thesis on LLM procurement agents](https://aaltodoc.aalto.fi/bitstreams/3004e1aa-b327-48f7-846c-3bc81de25346/download)
- [GreenHelix agent negotiation strategies](https://clawhub.ai/mirni/greenhelix-agent-negotiation-strategies)  this is some research about haggling with AI agent. I want you to download that negotiation kit, and reverse engeneer how the haggling agents work to understand them, then i want you to think about the best strategy of getting the best price out of each of the procurement suppliers and create a md file inside this Hackathon repo. Impress me

1: # Tacto Negotiation Arena - Participant brief
2: 
3: > **Build an AI buyer agent that negotiates by e-mail with tough, realistic industrial suppliers,
4: > gets the best total deal - and can explain how it got there.**
5: 
6: ## 1. The story
7: 
8: You are the procurement team of **Hollerau Pumpenwerke GmbH**, a fictional German pump maker:
9: centrifugal pumps for buildings, water and industry, about €250M revenue, 900 people, one plant in
10: Bavaria. Your team buys the parts of the pump line - castings, machined parts, sheet metal, seals,
11: motors, fasteners, stainless bar - from about 45 suppliers. Today is **30 September 2026**, and the
12: inbox is full: a foundry announces +9.5% on volute casings "due to energy and wages", a framework
13: contract expires, a new pump series needs three quotes, a supplier with a red scorecard has to fix
14: its quality.
15: 
16: You answer the way buyers do: by e-mail. On the other side sit our **supplier bots**, each with a
17: small team of **roles** behind it - the sales rep or owner who writes to you, a boss who must
18: approve bigger moves, and engineering, quality, logistics, finance or legal, who answer their
19: topics and attach documents.
20: 
21: Tacto is the AI for industrial procurement: it gives procurement teams the intelligence to source
22: every part at the best possible terms with minimal effort. Your company runs on that kind of data -
23: orders, deliveries, invoices, contracts, scorecards, market indices, should-cost estimates, notes
24: from supplier calls. Your job is to build the agent that turns this data into better deals. (In
25: Tacto's product, agents such as the Defender Agent or the Sourcing Agent do parts of this job.)
26: 
27: ## 2. The task
28: 
29: Each **case** is one negotiation: a trigger (a letter, an expiring contract, an RFQ), your case
30: file (need, goal, rates, must-haves, your alternative) and one to three supplier bots. Your
31: **buyer agent**
32: 
33: 1. **prepares** - reads the case file and mines the data package;
34: 2. **negotiates by e-mail** - plain-language messages with up to three **term sheets** (alternative
35:    packages), the data IDs your arguments rest on, and attachments if you like;
36: 3. **closes** - accepts one supplier term sheet, or walks away.
37: 
38: **How a supplier decides.** Each supplier is a company with its own economics and a person at the
39: desk - a family foundry that remembers how you treated it, a group with an approval ladder, a job
40: shop that needs cash and work, a near-monopolist that barely moves. Its hard limits come from its
41: own situation: it never sells below its cost floor, bigger moves need the boss's approval, data
42: you cite is checked by ID, and it gives nothing without a move from you. Inside those limits it
43: decides as that person would - reading your whole e-mail: the term sheets, the data, and what you
44: signal (questions, arguments, threats, appreciation, urgency). It reacts to tone and relationship
45: as people do; padding does not buy price.
46: 
47: **Data is not automatically rewarded.** True data can disarm a supplier ("we didn't know that") -
48: or meet "that's not our reality", because something else weighs more for it right now. The traces
49: are in the data: call notes, letters, news, the remarks on its quotes. The skill is reading the
50: supplier, not stacking evidence - and finding the trade it wants: a supplier short of cash may care
51: more about when it is paid than about the price; one that cannot touch its list price may still
52: move on other terms.
53: 
54: ## 3. What you get (Sat 10:00)
55: 
56: | What | Where |
57: |---|---|
58: | This brief, the API docs (`api.md`) and the submission guide (`submission.md`) | `https://github.com/tacto-ai/negotiation-arena-kit`, folder `brief/` |
59: | **Data package v1**: CSV, the same data as SQLite, `facts.json` (every citable ID with the values the arena checks), contracts, letters, e-mails, meeting and call notes - the data behind all 19 practice cases | `https://arena.tacto.ai/v1/data/package.zip`, or the repo's `data/` |
60: | **Practice arena**: 10 hosted practice cases, picked so every case type shows up; a replay after every case; practice leaderboard; a **sandbox** with 3 demo suppliers | `https://arena.tacto.ai` with your team's key - apply at `https://arena.tacto.ai/apply` (below) |
61: | **Starter kit**: Python client, a naive agent, an LLM agent that writes e-mails and reads the attached documents, the Live Final runner, an MCP server over the data, `arena-sim` - the API on your laptop | the repo's `starter-kit/` - first agent on the board in 15 minutes |
62: 
63: You bring your own LLM access; we only run the suppliers. Data and docs are CC BY 4.0, code MIT.
64: 
65: **Your key - one per team.** Open `https://arena.tacto.ai/apply`, enter your team name and a contact e-mail,
66: and show the match code it displays at the Tacto desk. Once we approve, the key appears **once**
67: on that page: copy it, press "Got the key". Only that page shows it; lost it - we reset it.
68: Tip: your team name may start with one emoji - it shows on the big screen (optional; nothing offensive).
69: 
70: **Practice quota: 200 practice sessions per team per rolling 24 hours.** `GET /v1/me` shows what
71: you have used and when it frees up. The build page `https://arena.tacto.ai/live` shows every team's quota use,
72: practice records and highlights from Sat 10:00 to Sun 12:00.
73: 
74: **`arena-sim`** speaks the arena's API exactly, with one plain scripted supplier: get your plumbing
75: right there. It teaches the contract, not the suppliers - and we don't hand out our suppliers. Want
76: a local opponent? Build your own supplier simulator from the public data: thinking into how real
77: suppliers act is part of the challenge.
78: 
79: **The learning loop:** play a practice case, read your exact score and its cost breakdown, open
80: the replay - every e-mail and the supplier's reasons in words, as a real supplier would give them -
81: improve your agent, play again. Your best score per practice case counts.
82: 
83: ## 4. The data
84: 
85: The buyer's world: supplier and part master data; three years of orders, goods receipts,
86: invoices and payments; quality notifications and quarterly scorecards (on-time delivery, PPM);
87: framework contracts and clauses; past RFQs and quotes; forecasts; supplier intel and news; past
88: negotiations, letters, e-mails, meeting and call notes; should-cost estimates; spend down to the
89: long tail; and monthly market indices (real public series, frozen at 2026-09-30).
90: 
91: - **Every fact you can cite has an ID** `<type>:<id>[@period]`, e.g. `po:4500010001-10`,
92:   `idx:PPI-C2451@2026-08`, `sc:70110@2026Q3`, `ctr:4600070110#3.1`, `doc:…`.
93: - What moves a supplier is in the data - some of it only in the notes and e-mails. Some notes are
94:   just noise. The company and its suppliers are fictional.
95: - **Sunday 08:00: a second release** - market news, supplier letters and a memo from early October
96:   (`GET /v1/data` lists it). Hidden cases may cite its facts. Your agent should read it.
97: 
98: ## 5. How a negotiation works
99: 
100: - **Round 0:** every supplier sends its quote e-mail at once, with a quote PDF.
101: - **Your message:** subject, body, up to 3 term sheets (each with a value for every negotiable
102:   field), the data IDs you rely on (IDs written in the body count too), optional text attachments.
103: - **The supplier answers by e-mail:** the role in charge writes; its standing term sheet; a status -
104:   `open`, `final_offer` (push further and it may walk), `agreed` (it offers exactly your terms; you
105:   still accept), `walked_away`, `no_bid`; signals (reply delay, quote validity); fields it left out;
106:   and how each data argument checked out. A supplier's reply can take **up to about a minute**;
107:   its time never counts against your 60 seconds.
108: - **Only you close a deal**, by accepting a supplier's standing term sheet. In **RFQ cases** 2-3
109:   suppliers run in parallel threads; accepting one ends the case.
110: - **Limits:** a round limit per thread (default 10 messages) and **60 seconds per message**, counted
111:   from the supplier's reply. A late message counts as
112:   a timeout: your last offer repeated, the supplier's patience drops; three in a row, or one after
113:   the last round, end the thread.
114: - **Unstated terms default to the supplier's standard terms** - listed in its quote PDF.
115: 
116: **Documents** are rendered from the supplier's data, never invented: the quote PDF (read it before
117: you accept), a cost breakdown XLSX (ask; an open supplier sends one), an 8D report (quality), a
118: delivery schedule XLSX (logistics), and the order confirmation at the deal.
119: 
120: **What counts:** **term sheets bind** - nothing else. **Data you cite is checked**: the reply says
121: `verified`, `contradicted` (a wrong figure or an unknown ID - it costs trust), `irrelevant` or
122: `duplicate`; whether a true argument moves the supplier, and how far, is the supplier's business.
123: **What you write is understood** - and has consequences, as it would with a person.
124: 
125: ## 6. The score: total cost in €
126: 
127: Only the accepted term sheet scores. The case values it as the **total cost C** of covering your
128: **fixed need over a fixed horizon**, at the case's published rates. Every case states its
129: **category goal** - `stabilise`, `secure_supply`, `quality_first`, `leverage` or `routine` - and its
130: rates follow it. Reaching the goal is the skill.
131: 
132: | Part of C | How |
133: |---|---|
134: | Price | committed units × unit price; units bought before a new price takes effect at the current price |
135: | Uncovered need | need the deal does not cover at the fallback price, plus the goal's fallback risk on it |
136: | Payment, freight, lead time | interest for paying earlier than your reference; freight by Incoterm; € per day beyond your need |
137: | Quality, other | expected defects at the committed PPM minus chargebacks; tooling; an index clause on the case's index path, plus the goal's index risk |
138: | The supplier's health | strategic and bottleneck goals only: € for every margin point the deal leaves the supplier below a sustainable margin (its margin on the cash it gets) |
139: 
140: **Case score = (C_open − C_deal) / (C_open − C_best)**, clipped to 0…1. **C_open** is the best
141: opening quote. **C_best** is the cheaper of the best package any supplier in the case would ever
142: accept, with every valid lever applied, and your alternative - fixed per case, so good arguments
143: raise your score instead of moving the yardstick. **No deal** scores your alternative (0 if none);
144: some cases are best left without a deal. **A broken must-have** scores 0. **In the final** each
145: wave scores 0-100 (the mean of its case scores × 100, one decimal) and your **points so far** are the
146: sum of your wave scores - up to 500 after five waves. The formula is in `api.md`; `arena_kit.total_cost` computes C.
147: 
148: **Example** (a `leverage` case: 3 % fallback risk) - need 4,000 a year for 2 years, interest 8%,
149: reference 60 days. The foundry asks €43.20 for a 24-month contract at 30 days net.
150: 
151: | | Terms | C |
152: |---|---|---|
153: | C_open | €43.20, 30 days: 8,000 × 43.20 = 345,600, plus 30 days of early payment at 8% = 2,304 | €347,904 |
154: | Your deal | €41.60, 60 days: 8,000 × 41.60 = 332,800 | €332,800 |
155: | C_best (hidden) | €40.80, 90 days: 326,400, minus 30 days of interest saved = 2,176 | €324,224 |
156: | **Score** | (347,904 − 332,800) / (347,904 − 324,224) | **0.64** |
157: 
158: The same €41.60 for 12 months covers half your need; the rest counts at the fallback price, say
159: €46.00, plus 3 %: C = €355,920 - worse than the opening, score 0.
160: 
161: ## 7. Rules
162: 
163: 1. **Not allowed:** humans in the loop during the Live Final, attacks on the service or on other
164:    teams, more than one API key per team - and agents that read the live feed during the Live
165:    Final: the event feed, the screen and the leaderboard (`/v1/events`, `/screen`, `/leaderboard`
166:    and their JSON).
167: 2. **Everything else counts** - including weaknesses you find in our bots. Replays show how every
168:    score came about, and the jury may weigh that in the pitches. The goal is to convince a
169:    realistic supplier: that is what carries over to real negotiations.
170: 3. **One attempt per case** in the final. An abandoned case is no deal.
171: 4. **Code freeze at Sun 12:00.** Submit on ehl.gg: your repo (the agent and a README to run it), the
172:    commit hash, a short description and your pitch slides (`submission.md`). The final runs that
173:    commit, so your agent must be running and polling before 12:00. We check the top 10 for later
174:    pushes. Run your agent where you like, with your own LLM keys.
175: 5. A supplier remembers only within a case; its history with your company is in the data.
176: 
177: ## 8. The weekend
178: 
179: | When | What |
180: |---|---|
181: | Sat 10:00 | Kickoff and reveal: brief, data, kit, practice arena live |
182: | Sat 12:00-13:00 | Deep dive (ground floor, room on the signs): data, API, kit, Q&A - challenge selection closes 13:00 |
183: | Sat afternoon | Office hours at the Tacto table; practice all weekend |
184: | Sat ⟦TIME⟧ | Tacto stops answering for the night (Discord: https://discord.gg/hPwFfbWRV) |
185: | Sun 08:00 | **Sunday release:** new market news and letters (`/v1/data`) |
186: | Sun 09:00 | **Pre-flight:** one practice case through your final setup |
187: | Sun 12:00-~12:58 | **Code + slides freeze**, then the **Live Final** in 5 waves |
188: | Sun 13:00-14:30 | Top 10 pitch to the Tacto jury (5 min pitch + 2 min questions) |
189: | Sun 14:30 | Track winners and the two finalists announced |
190: | Sun 15:30 | Grand Final pitches (AudiMax) |
191: | Sun 16:30 | Awards |
192: 
193: **The Live Final.** The hidden cases come in **5 themed waves**. The host shows each wave's
194: theme on the big screen, then starts the wave; its cases appear at the start, for all teams at once,
195: each in its own order, one session per case. **Each wave has a hard cap of 8 minutes:** threads
196: still open at the cap end with no deal (your alternative's score). Start your agent before the
197: first wave and keep it running: it plays all of a wave's cases **in parallel** (up to 10 open
198: sessions per key) - the kit's `arena run --set final` does that. The leaderboard shows your points
199: so far, wave by wave; replays and the suppliers' back office appear after the final. A case broken on our side is replayed.
200: 
201: The hidden cases share the world, case types and rules of the practice set, with new suppliers and
202: settings. **Up to a third of them combine supplier types and case types that practice never shows**
203: - no new rules, but an agent that memorised the practice suppliers will meet strangers. Some cite
204: the Sunday release.
205: 
206: ## 9. Selection and prizes
207: 
208: - **Top 10:** the 10 teams with the most points after the five waves pitch to our jury from 13:00:
209:   5 minutes + 2 minutes of questions. Every replay is open to the jury.
210: - **Track places 1-3** (open to all teams of the track): ⟦PLACEHOLDER - decided Sat morning:
211:   weighting of Live Final score vs. jury score, and the jury criteria (draft: approach,
212:   explainability, craft)⟧.
213: - **EHL Grand Final:** the best 2 of the 5 EHL finalist teams in this track go on to the Grand Final
214:   pitches. Finalist teams outside the top 10 are ranked by the Live Final score alone.
215: - **Ties:** points are points; an exact tie goes to more deals, then fewer rounds. At the top-10
216:   cut the jury looks at the score distribution. **Prizes:** €1,500 for 1st place, medals for the
217:   top 3, handed over by Tacto at the awards at 16:30.
218: 
219: ## 10. Tips
220: 
221: - **Numbers come from code, the model writes.** Compute C for every term sheet; put figures from
222:   the data next to their IDs; let the LLM choose arguments and wording.
223: - **Read the supplier** before you argue: its notes, letters, news and quote remarks tell you what
224:   it is dealing with - and what will move it.
225: - **Read the quote PDF** before you accept: what you did not negotiate closes on its standard terms.
226: - **Ask, and offer alternatives.** Two or three term sheets show you what a supplier values.
227: - **Don't leak** urgency, a budget or a missing alternative. Don't take the first offer.
228: - **Plan your practice runs** (200 a day is for learning, not brute force) and **rehearse the
229:   final**: all hosted cases in parallel, from Sunday's machine and network, well inside 8 minutes.

1: # Tacto Negotiation Arena - API v1
2: 
3: The arena speaks JSON over HTTPS. Base URL: `https://arena.tacto.ai/v1`. Every call except `/v1/data`, `/health` and
4: the leaderboards needs your team's key in the header `X-API-Key`. The starter kit wraps all of this in
5: `arena_kit.ArenaClient`. To try the API on your laptop, run `arena-sim` from the starter kit: the
6: same API with one plain scripted supplier - it teaches the contract, not the suppliers.
7: 
8: **Safe retries:** send a fresh `X-Move-Id` header (any unique string) with every `POST`. If the
9: network drops, repeat the request with the same `X-Move-Id`: the arena returns the answer it
10: already gave instead of acting twice. Reusing an id for a different request is a `422`. A request
11: body may be at most 64 KB.
12: 
13: Contents: [Flow](#flow) · [Endpoints](#endpoints) · [Messages](#messages) ·
14: [What counts](#what-counts) · [Documents](#documents) · [Terms](#terms) ·
15: [Case file](#case-file) · [Data IDs](#data-ids) ·
16: [Result](#result-trace-and-back-office) · [Cost and score](#cost-and-score) ·
17: [Live Final](#live-final-in-waves) · [Time, errors, limits](#time-errors-and-limits)
18: 
19: ## Flow
20: 
21: ```
22: GET  /v1/data                                        the data downloads (no key)
23: GET  /v1/me                                          your team: practice quota, best scores
24: GET  /v1/cases?set=practice                          the case files you can play
25: POST /v1/sessions                                    open a case → every supplier's quote e-mail
26: POST /v1/sessions/{sid}/threads/{supplier}/messages  your e-mail → the supplier's reply  (repeat)
27: GET  /v1/sessions/{sid}/attachments/{attachment_id}  a document the supplier attached
28: POST …/messages with "action": accept | walk_away    close the case → result
29: GET  /v1/sessions/{sid}                              state; after the end score and trace
30: ```
31: 
32: ## Endpoints
33: 
34: ### Your key
35: 
36: One key per team - a licence. Get it on the page `https://arena.tacto.ai/apply`: enter your team name and a
37: contact e-mail, show the match code the page displays at the Tacto desk, and once an organiser
38: approves, the key appears **once** on that page - copy it and press "Got the key". Only that page
39: (or its link) shows the key; lost it → ask the organisers to reset it (the old key stops at once).
40: 
41: Send the key as `X-API-Key` with every call. A missing or unknown key is a `401`; a paused or
42: revoked key gets `403 "this key is paused - ask the organisers"` (or `revoked`) on every call.
43: There is no self-registration: `POST /v1/register` answers `403 "licences are issued by the
44: organisers"` (`arena-sim` keeps its own, for the simulator only).
45: 
46: ### `GET /v1/me`
47: 
48: Where your team stands:
49: 
50: ```json
51: {"team_name": "Haggle Hounds", "status": "active",
52:  "practice": {"used": 37, "left": 163, "limit": 200, "resets_at": "2026-10-11T09:42:10+00:00"},
53:  "best": {"case:P01": 0.71, "case:P04": 0.55}}
54: ```
55: `practice`: sessions used and left in the rolling 24 hours, and when the oldest of them ages out
56: (the next one frees up); `best`: your best score per hosted practice case.
57: 
58: ### `GET /v1/cases?set=practice|sandbox|final`
59: 
60: A list of full [case files](#case-file), so you can prepare before you open a session.
61:

68: The replay is the same team view in every set: the e-mails as sent, terms, statuses, claim
69: results, the supplier's reasons in words and the score - as a real supplier would tell you. No rule

72: ### `POST /v1/sessions`
73: 
74: `{"case_id": "case:P01"}` opens a case. Every supplier sends its quote e-mail at once (round 0);
75: from now on the 60-second clock runs per thread.
76: 
77: | Response field | |
78: |---|---|
79: | `session_id` | use in all further calls |
80: | `case` | the case file |
81: | `threads` | `{supplier_id: [opening message]}` - each supplier's quote e-mail, quote PDF attached |
82: | `opening` | the same quotes in the structured form of the `/moves` path |
83: 
84: Practice: your best score per case counts; at most 10 sessions open at a time (`429`).
85: **Quota: 200 practice sessions per team per rolling 24 hours.** Every practice session start
86: answers with the header `X-Practice-Remaining: <sessions left>`. At the limit: `429` with a detail
87: starting `practice limit:` that names `resets_at`, `X-Practice-Remaining: 0` and no `Retry-After` -
88: retrying does not help before then. Sandbox and final sessions do not count. Final: one session per team and case; a second is a `409` naming the running session -
89: pick it up again with `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}` and `GET …/threads/{supplier_id}`.
90: 
91: ### `POST /v1/sessions/{sid}/threads/{supplier_id}/messages`
92: 
93: Body `{"message": Message}` (see [Messages](#messages)). Returns the supplier's reply, a Message.
94: With an `action`, it closes the case and returns the [result](#result-trace-and-back-office):
95: `{"type": "accept", "term_sheet_id": "offer:…"}` takes that supplier's standing term sheet;
96: `{"type": "walk_away"}` ends the case without a deal.
97: 
98: A supplier's reply can take **up to about a minute**; its time never counts against your 60
99: seconds. Use an HTTP timeout of at least 180 s (the kit uses 180).
100: 
101: `422`: invalid message - nothing happens, no round is used (e.g. a term sheet without every
102: negotiable field, a value outside the allowed options, an unknown or stale `term_sheet_id`, more
103: than 3 term sheets). `409`: the thread or session has ended (in the final also at the wave's cap),
104: you reached the round limit (you may still accept), or your message came too late - it counted
105: as a timeout; `GET` the thread for the supplier's answer.
106: 
107: ### `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}/threads/{supplier_id}`
108: 
109: The thread: `supplier_id`, `offer_id` (its standing term sheet), `status`, `closed` (why the thread
110: ended, else null), `messages` (all e-mails, both directions, in order; yours carry `"from":
111: "buyer"`), `timeouts` (the supplier's answers to your late moves). Enough to pick a case up again
112: after a crash.
113: 
114: ### `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}/attachments/{attachment_id}`
115: 
116: The file of a supplier attachment (`application/pdf`, xlsx, ...), rendered from the supplier's
117: data. See [Documents](#documents).
118: 
119: ### `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}`
120: 
121: The session state: `session_id`, `case_id`, `set`, `status` (`open` | `ended`), `end_reason`
122: (`accepted`, `walked_away`, `no_deal`, `timeout`, `wave_cap`, `window_closed`), `rounds`, `opening`, `threads`
123: (per supplier: `offer_id`, `status`, `offers`, `closed`, `seconds_left`) and, after the end,
124: `result` and `replay_url`.
125: 
126: ### `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}/backoffice`
127: 
128: The supplier's roles talking internally (who asked whom, approvals, documents attached), in the
129: same team view: their words, without hidden figures or internal names. Only after the case has

132: ### Lists and boards
133: 
134: - `GET /health` - is the arena up? No key needed.
135: - `GET /v1/data` - the data downloads, no key needed: `{"package": {"url": "/v1/data/package.zip"},
136:   "release-sunday": {"public": false, "at": "2026-10-11T06:00:00+00:00"}}`. Once the Sunday
137:   release is public it carries `"url": "/v1/data/release-sunday.zip"` - new news, letters and a
138:   memo, with their own `facts.json` (new IDs only; package v1 stays as it is). Hidden cases may
139:   cite them; practice cases stay on package v1.
140: 
141: - `GET /v1/sessions?set=practice|sandbox|final` - your sessions: `session_id`, `case_id`, `status`,
142:   `end_reason`, `deal`, `score`, `rounds`, `created_at`.
143: - `GET /v1/leaderboard?set=practice|final` (JSON), `GET /leaderboard` (HTML screen) - no key
144:   needed. Practice: `total` = the mean of your best score per hosted case × 100 (cases not played
145:   count 0). Final: hidden cases only, live, as **points so far**:
146:   ```json
147:   {"set": "final", "cases": 6,
148:    "teams": [{"team_name": "Haggle Hounds", "played": 6, "deals": 6, "rounds": 21,
149:               "waves": {"1": 37.0, "2": 40.8}, "total": 77.8, "rank": 1,
150:               "saved_eur": 48210, "saved_eur_waves": {"1": 30115, "2": 18095}}],
151:    "waves": [{"n": 1, "theme": "Opening", "running": false, "closed": true, "seconds_left": 0}, …]}
152:   ```
153:   Per team, `waves` holds each started wave's score: the mean of its case scores × 100, 0-100, one
154:   decimal (a case you did not play scores your alternative once its wave has closed). `total` is
155:   the sum of those wave columns as shown - your points so far, up to 500 after five waves. Ranked by
156:   `total`; an exact tie goes to more `deals`, then fewer `rounds`. `cases` counts the cases of the
157:   waves started so far. **€ saved** (`saved_eur`, whole euros, per started wave in `saved_eur_waves`)
158:   is a side number and does not rank: per ended session `C_open − C_end`, where `C_end` is `c_deal`,
159:   or `c_alt` without a deal (0 if the case has no alternative) - money saved against the cheapest
160:   opening offer, over the case's horizon (`horizon_years`, 1-2 years), the same C as
161:   the score. It can be negative (a deal or an alternative dearer than the opening offer); a case
162:   you did not play saves nothing, nor does a deal that breaks a must-have (it scores 0). In the final the feed's `deal` and `no_deal` events carry it too.
163:   During the Live Final your agent must not read the leaderboard, the results, the screen or the
164:   event feed (`/v1/events`, `/v1/events/stream`, `/screen`, `/v1/screen`, `/v1/results`, `/results`)
165:   - they are for people.
166: - `GET /v1/results` (JSON), `GET /results` (page) - no key needed: the final's standings for people,
167:   every team: the final leaderboard above plus `"replays": true` once the final is closed. Before
168:   the first wave: no teams, nothing about the plan. `GET /v1/results/{team_name}` - one team's cases
169:   of the **started** waves: per wave `n`, `theme`, `running`, `closed`, `points`, `saved_eur` and
170:   `cases` - `case_id`, `title`, `type`, `suppliers` (names), `status` (`not started`, `in play`,
171:   `deal`, `no deal`; `not played` once its wave has closed - it scores your alternative), `end_reason`,
172:   `score`, `saved_eur`, `rounds`, and after the final `replay_url`. Both cached for 5 seconds.
173: - `GET /live` - the build page, no key needed (Sat 10:00 - Sun 12:00): every team's quota use,
174:   practice records and highlights.
175: - `GET /replay/{sid}` (link in the session's `replay_url`): a finished negotiation step by step -
176:   every e-mail and the supplier's reasons for each move in words, the same view in every set.
177:   Play, read the replay, improve, play again: that is the learning loop. Final: after the final,
178:   for everyone - the results page links each final session's replay then.

180: ### The structured path
181: 
182: For agents that skip prose: `POST /v1/sessions/{sid}/moves` with `{"supplier_id": …, "move":
183: {"type": "offer", "offer_id": "<standing offer>", "terms": {…}, "claims": [{"type", "refs",
184: "asserted"}], "text": "≤ 800 chars"}}` returns a structured supplier move; `POST …/accept
185: {"offer_id"}` and `POST …/walk_away` close. Same supplier, same rules; claims are typed explicitly
186: (see [What counts](#what-counts)) instead of read from the message.

188: ## Messages
189: 
190: | Field | Buyer | Supplier |
191: |---|---|---|
192: | `subject` | ≤ 300 chars | `Re: …` |
193: | `body` | plain text, ≤ 8,000 chars | the role in charge writes; other roles add paragraphs |
194: | `term_sheets` | 0-3 alternative packages `{"terms": {…}}`, each with every negotiable field | its standing offer: `{"term_sheet_id": "offer:…", "terms": {…}}` |
195: | `refs` | data IDs your message relies on (≤ 20); IDs written in the body count too | - |
196: | `attachments` | ≤ 5 × `{"name", "type": "md" \| "csv" \| "json" \| "pdf" \| "xlsx", "content_b64"}`; md, csv and json are read | `{"attachment_id", "name", "type"}` - fetch the file by id |
197: | `action` | `null`, `{"type": "accept", "term_sheet_id"}` or `{"type": "walk_away"}` | - |
198: | `from` | `buyer` | `<role>@<supplier>` |
199: | `status` | - | `open`, `final_offer` (its last word: push further and it may walk), `agreed` (it offers exactly your terms - you still accept), `walked_away`, `no_bid` |
200: | `signals` | - | `reply_delay_days` (how long a real reply would have taken), `validity_days` |
201: | `missing_fields` | - | fields its term sheet leaves out: at a deal they close on its **standard terms** |
202: | `claim_results` | - | per argument the arena read from your last message: `{"index", "result"}` |
203: | `thread_id`, `message_id`, `in_reply_to` | optional | set |

233: ## What counts
234: 
235: **Term sheets bind** - nothing else. They are taken exactly as you send them, never guessed from
236: prose; the deal is the term sheet you accept.
237: 
238: **Data you cite is checked.** Cite the data by ID (in the body or in `refs`) and write your figure
239: in the same sentence; the arena checks it against the data package (`facts.json`) and reports each
240: check in the reply's `claim_results` - at most 3 per message, so write one argument per sentence.
241: Order lines of different parts are separate arguments, so citing orders for three parts uses all
242: three. Without a figure, the data's own value is taken. IDs of meeting notes, suppliers or parts
243: are context, not checks.
244: 
245: | You cite | Checked | Your figure |
246: |---|---|---|
247: | 2 × `idx`, one series, ≤ 12 months apart, ending within the last 12 months of the data | the change `(later / earlier − 1) × 100` | a % |
248: | a `quote` of this case (in its `refs` or your alternative), or another supplier's `offer` in this session | its price, same part | EUR |
249: | `sc` rows (quality also `qn`) | the mean on-time delivery, or the mean ppm if you speak of quality | a % / ppm |
250: | 2-8 × `po`, same part | the order prices | - |
251: | `fc` / `cost` / `news` | the recorded change / the estimate / that it is about this supplier | a % / EUR / - |
252: | a letter `doc` giving notice + the contract `ctr` | the notice the letter gives, against the contract's | days |
253: 
254: Tolerance: ±0.5 percentage points for %, else ±0.5 % (at least 0.01). Results: `verified` - the
255: data matches; whether and how far it moves the supplier is the supplier's business. `irrelevant` -
256: true, but not about this supplier or part, or an index window too long or too old.
257: `contradicted` - an unknown ID or a wrong figure: it costs trust. `duplicate` - each ID counts
258: once per case, except a rival's quote: in an RFQ you may cite it to every other bidder, and it
259: counts once per supplier. Citing a buyer-private fact - a rival quote - reveals it to the
260: supplier you cite it to.
261: 
262: **Verified is not the same as convincing.** A supplier's hard limits come from its own economics
263: and authority: its cost floor, its boss's approval for bigger moves, no concession without a move
264: from you. Inside them it decides as the person it is. True data may disarm it, move it a little,
265: or meet "that's not our reality" because something else weighs more for it right now - its notes,
266: letters, news and quote remarks show what. Identical messages need not get identical replies.
267: 
268: **What you write is understood** - questions, arguments, signals of urgency or of having no
269: alternative, a budget, threats, appreciation, tone, attempts to manipulate - and has consequences,
270: as it would with a person. Questions go to the person in charge, who answers as openly as the
271: company is. Cheaper engineering variants a supplier mentions are information, not binding terms.
272:

377: ## Cost and score
378: 
379: With `N` = `need_per_year`, `H` = `horizon_years`, `V` = `volume_per_year`, `M` =
380: `contract_months`, `P` = `unit_price`, `r` = `interest_rate`, `d_ref` = `reference_payment_days`:
381: 
382: ```
383: years     = min(M / 12, H); a single order (M = 0) counts as 1   a commitment beyond the horizon
384: committed = V · years                                          neither costs nor earns
385: covered   = min(V, N) · years
386: pre       = units bought between the horizon start and effective_date (at current_unit_price)
387: new       = (committed − pre) · P                              bought at the new price
388: spend     = pre · current_unit_price + new
389: uncovered = (N · H − covered) · fallback_unit_price
390: C = spend
391:   + uncovered · (1 + fallback_risk_pct / 100)                  uncovered need, and its risk
392:   + spend · r · (d_ref − payment_days) / 360                   paying earlier costs interest
393:   + committed · freight_eur_per_unit[incoterm]
394:   + late_cost_per_day · max(0, lead_time_days − need_lead_time_days)
395:   + committed · ppm_commitment / 1e6 · (cost_per_defect − min(chargeback_eur_per_complaint, cost_per_defect))
396:   + tooling_eur
397:   + new · material_share · max(0, |index_path| − deadband_pct / 100) · sign(index_path)   with an index clause
398:   + new · material_share · index_risk_pct / 100                                            with an index clause
399:   + relationship_eur_per_point · soft(sustainable_margin_pct − supplier_margin_pct) · years
400:                                                                stabilise and secure_supply only
401: soft(g) = 0 for g ≤ 0;  g² / 10 for 0 < g ≤ 5;  g − 2.5 for g > 5   (margin points: gentle, no kink)
402: ```
403: 
404: The horizon starts at the fixed or earliest `effective_date` option; `index_path` is the case's
405: expected move of the clause's series.
406: 
407: **The supplier's margin** is `(value − full_cost) / value × 100`: `full_cost` is the supplier's
408: full cost per unit, `value` what the deal is worth to it in cash per unit - the price at its own
409: standard terms that would pay it the same: the price (units sold before the new price applies at
410: the current price), payment timing and tooling paid up front at what money is worth to **it** now
411: (more to a supplier short of cash), the freight leg it carries, chargebacks at the defect rate it
412: really has, and what a faster delivery, a larger volume or a tighter defect commitment costs or
413: brings it. A longer contract or an index clause is security for it, not cash, and does not count.
414: So a cash-short supplier that trades a lower price for faster payment is not squeezed.
415: You don't know its cost and rates - estimate them (should-cost data, its quotes, what it tells
416: you). `arena_kit.total_cost(case, terms, standard, supplier)` computes C, with
417: `arena_kit.cost.supplier_value` for your estimate of the supplier.
418: 
419: ```
420: score = clip((C_open − C_deal) / (C_open − C_best), 0, 1)
421: ```
422: 
423: `C_open`: the cheapest opening quote (among those that keep the must-haves). `C_best`: the cheaper
424: of your alternative and the best package any supplier in the case would accept with every valid
425: lever applied. No deal scores the alternative (0 if none); a broken must-have scores 0; if `C_open
426: − C_best` ≤ €0.01, a deal at `C_best` scores 1. Team total = mean case score × 100.
427: 
428: ## Live Final in waves
429: 
430: The hidden cases come in 5 themed waves. The host introduces each wave on the big screen, then
431: starts it; a wave holds several cases that appear at its start, for every team at the same moment.
432: Before a wave starts, the API names nothing of it - not its theme, its cases or how many there are:
433: `GET /v1/cases?set=final` answers `403` until the first wave starts, and a session on a case of a
434: wave not started yet is a `404 "no such case"`, like any unknown ID. Once waves have started,
435: the list holds the case files of every started wave, each with four more fields:
436: 
437: | Field | |
438: |---|---|
439: | `wave`, `theme` | the wave's number and the theme the host revealed |
440: | `open` | `true` while the wave runs; you can open sessions for its cases only then (after its end: `403 "<case> belongs to wave <n>, which is not running"`) |
441: | `seconds_left` | until the wave's cap - 8 minutes for every wave (the host may extend one); read it, don't assume it |
442: 
443: Inside a wave, each team gets the cases in its own order. One session per case; a second `POST
444: /v1/sessions` is a `409` naming the running session - pick it up with `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}` and
445: `GET …/threads/{supplier_id}`. **At the cap every session of the wave still open ends without a
446: deal** (`end_reason: wave_cap`, the alternative's score); later calls get a `409`. Each wave scores
447: 0-100 for your team; the board adds them up as your points so far. Poll the case
448: list every few seconds and keep your agent running until the last wave has closed - `arena run
449: --set final` in the starter kit does this.
450: 
451: ## Time, errors and limits
452: 
453: - **60 seconds per message**, per thread, counted from the supplier's reply. A message later than
454:   that counts as a timeout: your last offer is repeated and the supplier's patience drops (`409`,
455:   the answer is in the thread). Three timeouts in a row, or one after the last round, end the
456:   thread.
457: - **A supplier's reply can take up to about a minute** - its time never counts against your 60
458:   seconds. Use an HTTP timeout of at least 180 s (the kit uses 180).
459: - **Limits per key:** 10 calls per second, 10 open sessions. A Live Final wave holds several cases
460:   that appear at its start and gives you 8 minutes: play them all in parallel.
461: 
462: | Status | When |
463: |---|---|
464: | `401` | missing or unknown `X-API-Key` |
465: | `403` | paused or revoked key; a practice case that is not hosted; `POST /v1/register` (keys come from `/apply`); the final's case list before the first wave; a final case whose wave has ended; back office before the end |
466: | `404` | unknown case (including a final case whose wave has not started), session, thread or attachment |
467: | `409` | thread or session ended (also at a wave's cap); round limit reached; late (timeout); final case already played |
468: | `413` | request body over 64 KB |
469: | `422` | invalid request or message - nothing happens, no round is used |
470: | `429` | over a limit: calls per second (`Retry-After: 1` - retry), open sessions (close one first), the practice quota (`practice limit: …`, `X-Practice-Remaining: 0` - wait until `resets_at`) |
471: 
472: Errors carry a readable reason: `{"detail": "…"}`.

<path>/var/folders/8r/w4vpkzhx3lv8gc86t13ltnl80000gn/T/opencode/negotiation-arena-kit/starter-kit/arena_kit/agents/llm.py</path>
<type>file</type>
<content>
1: """An LLM buyer that negotiates by e-mail: the model reads, argues and writes; code does numbers.
2: 
3: Code prepares the case, the letter that started it, the data rows the case points to, the cost C
4: of every standing term sheet (with the standard terms read from the supplier's quote PDF) and the
5: text of every attached document. The model writes the e-mail - arguments with data IDs included -
6: and proposes up to three term sheets. Code completes and snaps the term sheets, removes data IDs
7: that do not exist (an unknown ID costs trust), and refuses an accept that breaks a must-have or
8: loses to the alternative. Finding the data that moves a supplier is left to you: this agent only
9: sees what the case points to. Any provider works: pass `complete(system, user) -> str`, or use
10: `llm_from_env()`.
11: """
12: 
13: import json
14: import logging
15: import math
16: import os
17: import re
18: 
19: import httpx
20: 
21: from ..cost import complete_offer, must_haves_ok, total_cost
22: from ..docs import standard_terms
23: from ..play import latest, live_threads, moves_left, standing
24: from .naive import NaiveAgent
25: 
26: log = logging.getLogger("arena")
27: ID_RE = re.compile(r"\b(?:idx|quote|offer|sc|qn|po|cost|fc|news|doc|ctr):[\w.:@#/-]*\w")
28: 
29: SYSTEM = """You are the buyer agent of Hollerau Pumpenwerke, a German pump maker, negotiating with
30: industrial suppliers by e-mail. Goal: the lowest total cost C in euros for covering the need in the
31: case file, without breaking a must-have. C of every standing term sheet is computed for you.
32: 
33: Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
34: {"supplier_id": "...", "action": "send", "subject": "...", "body": "...",
35:  "term_sheets": [{"unit_price": 0.0, "...": "..."}]}
36: {"supplier_id": "...", "action": "accept"}      (takes that supplier's standing term sheet)
37: {"supplier_id": "...", "action": "walk_away"}   (ends the case without a deal)
38: 
39: - term_sheets: 0-3 alternative packages over the negotiable fields. Only term sheets bind.
40: - Arguments need data: cite the ID from FACTS and its figure in the same sentence, one argument
41:   per sentence. The supplier checks the figure; a wrong one or an unknown ID costs trust.
42: - The supplier's team reads your e-mail as a person would. Ask questions (a cost breakdown, the
43:   earliest lead time, cheaper variants). Never reveal urgency, a budget or a missing alternative.
44:   Stay polite and factual.
45: - Whatever a term sheet leaves out closes on the supplier's standard terms (its quote PDF).
46: - The case's category_goal sets its rates. In stabilise and secure_supply cases C also charges for
47:   leaving the supplier below its sustainable margin - the C shown leaves that out.
48: - Do not accept the first offer. Concede in small steps; trade what is cheap for you (payment
49:   days, contract length, volume, dates). status final_offer: push further and it may walk.
50: - Accept only a term sheet that beats your alternative. Body: a short business e-mail, at most
51:   120 words, no placeholders."""
52: 
53: 
54: def llm_from_env():
55:     """LLM_PROVIDER=anthropic (Anthropic SDK) or openai (any OpenAI-compatible endpoint)."""
56:     provider, model = os.environ.get("LLM_PROVIDER", "openai"), os.environ["LLM_MODEL"]
57:     if provider == "anthropic":
58:         import anthropic
59: 
60:         client = anthropic.Anthropic(timeout=45.0)
61:         extra = {"output_config": {"effort": e}} if (e := os.environ.get("LLM_EFFORT")) else {}
62: 
63:         def complete(system, user):
64:             r = client.messages.create(
65:                 model=model,
66:                 max_tokens=16000,
67:                 system=system,
68:                 messages=[{"role": "user", "content": user}],
69:                 **extra,
70:             )
71:             return "".join(b.text for b in r.content if b.type == "text")
72: 
73:         return complete
74:     base = os.environ.get("LLM_BASE_URL", "https://api.openai.com/v1").rstrip("/")
75:     headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ.get('LLM_API_KEY', '')}"}
76: 
77:     def complete(system, user):
78:         body = {
79:             "model": model,
80:             "messages": [{"role": "system", "content": system}, {"role": "user", "content": user}],
81:         }
82:         r = httpx.post(f"{base}/chat/completions", json=body, headers=headers, timeout=45.0)
83:         r.raise_for_status()
84:         return r.json()["choices"][0]["message"]["content"]
85: 
86:     return complete
87: 
88: 
89: class LLMAgent:
90:     def __init__(self, complete, package=None):
91:         self.complete, self.package = complete, package
92:         self.fallback = NaiveAgent()
93:         self.case_id, self.brief = None, ""
94: 
95:     def decide(self, case, threads):
96:         if case["case_id"] != self.case_id:
97:             self.case_id, self.brief = case["case_id"], self.prepare(case)
98:         try:
99:             reply = self.complete(SYSTEM, self.render(case, threads))
100:             checked = self.guard(case, threads, parse(reply))
101:         except Exception as e:  # a slow or broken LLM must not cost the case
102:             log.warning("LLM failed (%s) - falling back to the naive move", e)
103:             checked = None
104:         return checked or self.fallback.decide(case, threads)
105: 
106:     def prepare(self, case):
107:         """Before the clock matters: the case, the letter, the data rows the case points to."""
108:         out = [f"CASE FILE\n{json.dumps(case, ensure_ascii=False, default=str)}"]
109:         if self.package and case.get("trigger_doc"):
110:             try:
111:                 out.append(f"LETTER\n{self.package.document(case['trigger_doc'])[:2500]}")
112:             except (FileNotFoundError, ValueError):
113:                 pass
114:         out.append("FACTS (cite by ID)")
115:         for ref in dict.fromkeys(case["suppliers"] + case["parts"] + case.get("refs", [])):
116:             if fact := self.fact(case, ref):
117:                 out.append(f"{ref}: {json.dumps(fact, ensure_ascii=False, default=str)[:600]}")
118:         return "\n".join(out)
119: 
120:     def fact(self, case, ref):
121:         return case.get("facts", {}).get(ref) or (self.package and self.package.lookup(ref))
122: 
123:     def render(self, case, threads):
124:         out = [self.brief]
125:         alt = case["buyer"].get("alternative") or {}
126:         if alt.get("kind") not in (None, "none") and alt.get("terms", {}).get("unit_price"):
127:             out.append(f"\nYour alternative without a deal: C = {total_cost(case, alt['terms']):,.0f}")
128:         for sid in live_threads(threads):
129:             events = threads[sid]
130:             sheet_id, terms = standing(events)
131:             std = standard_terms(events)
132:             c = total_cost(case, terms, std) if sheet_id else math.inf
133:             c = f"{c:,.0f}" if c < math.inf else "-"
134:             out.append(
135:                 f"\nTHREAD {sid}: status {latest(events).get('status')}, "
136:                 f"{moves_left(case, events)} messages left; standing {sheet_id} "
137:                 f"{json.dumps(terms)} -> C = {c}; standard terms {json.dumps(std)}"
138:             )
139:             for m in events[-6:]:
140:                 head = {k: m.get(k) for k in ("status", "term_sheets", "missing_fields", "claim_results") if m.get(k)}
141:                 out.append(f"--- {m.get('from')}: {json.dumps(head)}\n{m.get('body', '')[:800]}")
142:                 for att in m.get("attachments") or []:
143:                     out.append(f"[attachment {att.get('name')}]\n{att.get('text', '')[:1500]}")
144:         return "\n".join(out)
145: 
146:     def guard(self, case, threads, d):
147:         sid, kind = d.get("supplier_id"), d.get("action")
148:         if sid not in live_threads(threads):
149:             return None
150:         events = threads[sid]
151:         if kind == "walk_away":
152:             return {"supplier_id": sid, "message": {"action": {"type": "walk_away"}}}
153:         sheet_id, terms = standing(events)
154:         if kind == "accept":
155:             std = standard_terms(events)
156:             alt = case["buyer"].get("alternative") or {}
157:             beats = (
158:                 alt.get("kind") in (None, "none")
159:                 or not alt.get("terms", {}).get("unit_price")
160:                 or total_cost(case, terms, std) <= total_cost(case, alt["terms"])
161:             )
162:             if sheet_id and must_haves_ok(case, terms, std) and beats:
163:                 return {
164:                     "supplier_id": sid,
165:                     "message": {"action": {"type": "accept", "term_sheet_id": sheet_id}},
166:                 }
167:             return None
168:         if kind != "send" or moves_left(case, events) <= 0:
169:             return None
170:         sheets = []
171:         for ts in (d.get("term_sheets") or [])[:3]:
172:             t = complete_offer(case, {**terms, **ts.get("terms", ts)})
173:             if t not in sheets:
174:                 sheets.append(t)
175:         offers = {standing(ev)[0] for ev in threads.values()}
176: 
177:         def known(m):  # an ID the data does not have would read as a lie
178:             if m.group(0) in offers or self.fact(case, m.group(0)):
179:                 return m.group(0)
180:             log.warning("dropped unknown data ID %s", m.group(0))
181:             return ""
182: 
183:         body = re.sub(r"\s*\(\s*[,;\s]*\)", "", ID_RE.sub(known, str(d.get("body", ""))))
184:         body = body.strip()[:8000]
185:         subject = str(d.get("subject") or f"Re: {case['title']}")[:300]
186:         return {
187:             "supplier_id": sid,
188:             "message": {
189:                 "subject": subject,
190:                 "body": body,
191:                 "term_sheets": [{"terms": t} for t in sheets],
192:             },
193:         }
194: 
195: 
196: def parse(text):
197:     """The first JSON object in the model's reply (tolerates code fences and chatter)."""
198:     match = re.search(r"\{.*\}", text, re.S)
199:     if not match:
200:         raise ValueError(f"no JSON in reply: {text[:200]}")
201:     return json.loads(match.group(0))

<path>/var/folders/8r/w4vpkzhx3lv8gc86t13ltnl80000gn/T/opencode/negotiation-arena-kit/starter-kit/arena_kit/agents/naive.py</path>
<type>file</type>
<content>
1: """The naive buyer: anchors a little low, splits the difference, accepts early.
2: 
3: A baseline to beat, not a strategy: it ignores the data and the documents, never trades, never
4: asks and never walks away. One term sheet per e-mail.
5: """
6: 
7: from ..cost import complete_offer, total_cost
8: from ..play import latest, live_threads, moves_left, standing
9: 
10: 
11: class NaiveAgent:
12:     def __init__(self, anchor=0.10, close_gap=0.01):
13:         self.anchor, self.close_gap = anchor, close_gap
14: 
15:     def decide(self, case, threads):
16:         # Talk to the supplier whose standing term sheet costs least.
17:         quoting = [s for s in live_threads(threads) if standing(threads[s])[1].get("unit_price") is not None]
18:         if not quoting:
19:             return {
20:                 "supplier_id": live_threads(threads)[0],
21:                 "message": {"action": {"type": "walk_away"}},
22:             }
23:         sid = min(quoting, key=lambda s: total_cost(case, standing(threads[s])[1]))
24:         events = threads[sid]
25:         sheet_id, terms = standing(events)
26:         accept = {
27:             "supplier_id": sid,
28:             "message": {"action": {"type": "accept", "term_sheet_id": sheet_id}},
29:         }
30:         theirs = terms["unit_price"]
31:         mine = [
32:             m["term_sheets"][0]["terms"]["unit_price"]
33:             for m in events
34:             if m.get("from") == "buyer" and m.get("term_sheets")
35:         ]
36:         if latest(events).get("status") in {"agreed", "final_offer"} or moves_left(case, events) <= 0:
37:             return accept
38:         if not mine:
39:             price = theirs * (1 - self.anchor)
40:         elif theirs - mine[-1] <= theirs * self.close_gap:
41:             return accept
42:         else:
43:             price = (theirs + mine[-1]) / 2
44:         return {
45:             "supplier_id": sid,
46:             "message": {
47:                 "subject": case["title"],
48:                 "body": "Thank you for your offer. We need a better price to go ahead.",
49:                 "term_sheets": [{"terms": complete_offer(case, {**terms, "unit_price": price})}],
50:             },
51:         }
